root_cause: Cable-2 sense corridor is fragmented by foreign signal intrusion: /SENSEC2_LO has 23 foreign crosses and splits into 2 islands; /SENSEC2_HI has 5 foreign crosses and also splits into 2 islands. This fragmentation reduces effective copper cross-section on both cable-2 sense nets, triggering FEM over-temp flags on those nets and driving the bulk of the 44 structural DRC violations. Two ratlines remain unconnected. Kelvin gates pass (kelvin_ok=true, kelvin_unrouted=0), so this is a routing deficiency — foreign signals freely traverse the cable-2 corridor rather than being routed around it. Cable-1 corridor is clean (SENSEC1_HI/LO both 1 island). The corridor-avoid lever fires deterministically from pour_clipped_nets=['/SENSEC2_HI','/SENSEC2_LO'] and should reroute offending foreign nets around the cable-2 band; combined with increased router passes this should close most DRC and the 2 open ratlines.
reasoning: kelvin_ok=true rules out a T0/GR-02 placement trigger. The pour fragmentation is squarely a routing problem: 23 foreign crosses on SENSEC2_LO is severe and the deterministic corridor-avoid lever already has the right target from clipped_nets. The FEM over-temp on SENSEC2_HI confirms the fragmented pour is thermally under-capacity, which will self-correct once the pour is no longer clipped. No placement change is warranted — cable-1 routing clean with a single island on both HI and LO demonstrates the placement geometry is viable; cable-2 just needs its corridor cleared of foreign traffic.

proposed_lever.detail: Corridor-avoid lever fires deterministically from pour_clipped_nets. Enforce a keepout band spanning the full cable-2 corridor (both HI and LO sides) so FR routes the 23 offending foreign signal nets around the corridor rather than through it. Pair with a bump in router passes/opt_time to close the 2 open ratlines.
